description:
The plot illustrates the relationship between initial confidence and three accuracy metrics. The x-axis is labeled “Initial Confidence” and has a linear scale ranging from 0.91 to 0.99, with tick labels at intervals of 0.01. The y-axis is labeled “Accuracy” and has a linear scale ranging from 0.0 to 1.0, with tick labels at intervals of 0.2. 

The “Final Accuracy” is represented by a blue line with circular markers and error bars. This line begins at approximately 0.83 at an initial confidence of 0.91, reaches a peak of approximately 0.86 at an initial confidence of 0.94, and ends at approximately 0.82 at an initial confidence of 0.99. The “Δ Accuracy” is represented by an orange line with diamond markers and error bars, starting at approximately 0.35 at an initial confidence of 0.91, rising to approximately 0.48 at an initial confidence of 0.95, and decreasing to approximately 0.18 at an initial confidence of 0.99. Finally, the “Initial Accuracy” is represented by a green line with square markers and error bars, beginning at approximately 0.22 at an initial confidence of 0.91, increasing to approximately 0.43 at an initial confidence of 0.95, and ending at approximately 0.31 at an initial confidence of 0.99.
